profiles.summary: The endpoint still reports reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb (celo-reth v1.0.10, revm-interpreter 35.0.1, revm-bytecode 10.0.0, ruint 1.20.0) and, on a minority of requests (34 of 201 pinned batches), the unsupported op-geth c7ed55b8. No celo-reth release after v1.0.10 exists. The interpreter that celo-kona main will ship (revm-interpreter 42.0.0, revm-bytecode 42.0.0) was diffed against 35.0.1 and changes no arithmetic, comparison, shift, signed, jump, memory or copy result. The battery, the targeted vectors and both script sets pass today, the battery also pinned to the celo-reth backend, and all 403 mined liquidity removals since deployment were recomputed from parent-block state.

deltas.delta: celo-kona main locks revm 42.0.1, revm-interpreter 42.0.0, revm-bytecode 42.0.0, ruint 1.20.0, alloy-primitives 1.7.3, fixed-cache 0.1.10 and celo-org/reth 4e0169d3 (reth-revm 2.5.2). The tag celo/reth-v1.0.10 still locks revm-interpreter 35.0.1 and revm-bytecode 10.0.0 from celo-org/revm bd28f94. Tags celo/reth-v1.0.11, v1.0.12, v1.1.0, v1.1.0-rc.1, v1.2.0 and v2.0.0 return 404.

Diff of the published crates revm-interpreter 35.0.1 and 42.0.0: arithmetic.rs, bitwise.rs, i256.rs, control.rs, memory.rs, system.rs and stack.rs change only the instruction signature (functions now return a Result instead of calling halt) and the internal stack helpers. Every arithmetic body, the shift and BYTE clamps, SIGNEXTEND, the signed division and remainder, the JUMP and JUMPI target check and the MCOPY and CALLDATACOPY resize are the same expressions. The SHL, SHR and SAR spec check moved from CONSTANTINOPLE to PETERSBURG, which is active on Celo either way.

revm-bytecode 10.0.0 (Celo today) advances the jump analysis pointer with an unchecked add past the end of the code when the code ends in a truncated PUSH (src/legacy/analysis.rs line 30); 42.0.0 replaces it with wrapping_add. The PoolManager's 24,009 byte runtime code on Celo ends on a complete instruction (the last opcode, EXP at offset 24,008, ends exactly at the code end; 610 JUMPDEST bytes), so its own analysis never takes that path.

Celo's hardfork configuration in celo-kona main (crates/kona/registry/etc/configs.json) ends at jovian_time 1774958788 for mainnet and has no Karst or Lagoon time. CLZ (0x1e) placed in code by state override is refused on both backends today (celo-reth: EVM error NotActivated; op-geth: invalid opcode CLZ).

profiles.summary: Celo ended support for op-geth on mainnet on 22 July 2026, so celo-reth alone produces and validates blocks. The transient storage difference between the two clients after the fee currency debit (L-256, L-343) therefore concerns a follower that may follow the wrong chain, not the block producer.

deltas.delta: Celo's notice says support for op-geth ended on mainnet on 22 July 2026, op-reth is the supported execution client, and a node still running op-geth can follow the wrong chain.

profiles.summary: Nothing new on CELO as gas token or on fee currencies. Karst still has no Celo date, so the EIP-7825 transaction gas cap is not scheduled in code.

Nothing new on the transfer precompile or the core contracts. celo-revm v1.0.10 and main build the instruction table with EthInstructions::new_mainnet_with_spec from the context spec and add no instruction of their own.

deltas.delta: crates/celo-revm/src/evm.rs at celo/reth-v1.0.10 derives the instruction table from the context spec; its comment records that an earlier revision hardcoded the OSAKA table. Opcode activation is checked inside each handler against the runtime spec (revm-interpreter 35.0.1 bitwise.rs line 23, check! OSAKA in clz), so the table choice never enabled CLZ; the live probe confirms it is refused.

profiles.summary: The endpoint reports reth/v2.3.0-f60420a xlayer/v0.0.7. A final tag v0.0.7.3 now exists beside v0.0.7.3-rc.1; every xlayer-reth tag and main lock the same EVM crates (revm 40.0.3, revm-interpreter 37.0.3, revm-bytecode 11.0.1, ruint 1.18.0), and op-revm in okx/optimism main uses the stock instruction table. The battery, the targeted vectors and both script sets pass today.

deltas.delta: xlayer-reth tags v0.0.7 and v0.0.7.3 pin okx/reth 81573d2c, while v0.0.7.3-rc.1, main and okx/optimism main pin okx/reth f60420aa, the revision named in the endpoint's version string. The EVM crates are identical in all four locks.

Diff of the published crates revm-interpreter 37.0.3 and 42.0.0: no instruction file of arithmetic, bitwise, control, memory, stack or system changes; host.rs changes the SSTORE cold-load skip threshold from the additional cold cost to the full cold cost, which never applies because the EIP-2200 stipend check and the static charge leave more than 2,200 gas at that point (host.rs lines 198-215). 43.0.0 makes resize_memory return MemoryOOG when the memory buffer refuses to grow; SharedMemory's resize always reports success (shared_memory.rs lines 122-125), so nodes on SharedMemory are unaffected.
revm-bytecode 11.0.1 carries the same unchecked pointer add for a trailing truncated PUSH as Celo's 10.0.0. The X Layer PoolManager code also ends on a complete instruction.

profiles.summary: The node binary uses the stock OpNode components with only the payload builder replaced, so followers and eth_call execute through the same op-revm path. The xlayer-reth chain spec on main still ends at Jovian.

deltas.delta: bin/node/src/main.rs of v0.0.7.3 builds the node from op_node.components() with a custom XLayerPayloadServiceBuilder carrying the bridge intercept configuration; execution of received blocks uses the stock OP executor.
crates/chainspec/src/xlayer_mainnet.rs on main configures forks up to Jovian (timestamp 1764691201) with no Karst entry.

profiles.summary: Nothing new on OKB as gas token or the gasless list.
Nothing new on predeploys or precompiles. op-revm in okx/optimism main keeps the stock precompile sets per OP spec, with Karst limits defined but no Karst activation on X Layer.

cleared.check: Upcoming celo-reth interpreter: does revm-interpreter 42.0.0 (celo-kona main) change any instruction result relative to 35.0.1 (celo-reth v1.0.10) for MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP, JUMPI, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion or CALLDATALOAD.
cleared.result: No. The diff of the two published crates is a refactor of the instruction signature and stack helpers; every computing expression is unchanged and ruint stays at 1.20.0 in both locks, so FullMath, TickMath, BitMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath and TickBitmap get the same words.

cleared.check: Jump destination analysis in revm-bytecode 10.0.0 (Celo), 11.0.1 (X Layer) and 42.0.0 (celo-kona main), including the trailing PUSH pointer fix of 42.0.0.
cleared.result: Safe for the PoolManager. 10.0.0 and 11.0.1 differ only in const qualifiers of the jump map; 42.0.0 changes only the pointer arithmetic for a PUSH whose immediate runs past the end of the code. The deployed PoolManager on both chains ends on a complete instruction, so the case cannot arise for it, and for any other contract the bytes past its end hold no JUMPDEST.

leads.question: When celo-kona tags the first celo-reth release from main (revm-interpreter 42.0.0, revm-bytecode 42.0.0, celo-org/reth 4e0169d3), do the battery, targeted vectors, both script sets and removals.py still pass on its backend, and is keccak-cache-global enabled in that binary?
leads.why: The block producer's EVM crates move by seven major versions; the reading found no change in results, which a run must confirm.

leads.question: Why do the final tags v0.0.7 and v0.0.7.3 pin okx/reth 81573d2c while the endpoint and v0.0.7.3-rc.1 run f60420aa, and what differs between the two okx/reth revisions in the engine, execution cache and state root code?
leads.why: The EVM crates are the same, but the sequencer and the public endpoint may run different reth revisions of the block pipeline.

leadResults.answer: The gitlink of deps/optimism cannot be read without the GitHub API. Indirect evidence: xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3-rc.1 and main lock okx/reth f60420aa, the same revision okx/optimism main locks and the endpoint names, and both lock op-revm 20.0.0 and alloy-op-evm 0.32.0 as path crates with revm 40.0.3. okx/optimism main's alloy-op-evm block executor has the post-exec (SDM) code that upstream gates after Karst; no block access list type appears in its OpTxResult. Operator-level lead in any case (F-133 is information).

Still no tagged celo-reth release after v1.0.10. celo-kona main now locks revm-interpreter 42.0.0 from crates.io; its instruction files differ from 35.0.1 only in signatures, and celo-revm main still builds the stock instruction table from the context spec. The battery, targeted set and both script sets pass on forno today. Open until a release ships.

No release from main yet. celo-kona main locks alloy-primitives 1.7.3 and fixed-cache 0.1.10 (v1.0.10 locks 1.6.0 and 0.1.8). Whether the binary enables keccak-cache-global is decided by the release build and could not be read; the cache compares full keys (OPCODES.md, cycle 11). Duplicate of L-754.

Same state as L-639: revm-interpreter 42.0.0 is on main only; the diff against 35.0.1 shows no result change, and today's battery, targeted and script runs pass on forno including the battery pinned to celo-reth.

Celo ended support for op-geth on mainnet on 22 July 2026 (docs.celo.org op-geth deprecation notice), so celo-reth produces blocks. Its transfer precompile guards were read in cycles 6 and 11 and the op-geth guards in cycle 15; both match.

Only celo-reth produces and validates Celo blocks since 22 July 2026, and it clears the debit's transient storage before the main call. The op-geth behaviour concerns an unsupported follower. The PoolManager is unaffected on either client because its lock is closed and its deltas are zero outside unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), and only governance listed fee currencies run in the debit (actor governance).

Operator-level. The node binary uses stock OpNode execution with a custom payload builder; every xlayer-reth lock has revm 40.0.3, and 3,010 mined swaps replay to the unit. The sequencer's build cannot be read from chain data.

All 403 mined removals since deployment recomputed from parent-block storage: 399 match both currencies to the unit, principal and fees included, 1 native pool matches on the ERC-20 side, 3 could only be computed (hooked pool or earlier event of the pool in the block). No mismatch.

Answered with L-256: celo-reth is the only supported client since 22 July 2026 (both forno backends answer, but op-geth is a follower Celo says may follow the wrong chain). A fee currency that syncs during the debit would need governance listing, and on celo-reth its transient writes do not reach the main call.
